title: Biology — Mission 1: The Division Anomaly
description: Cells in the greenhouse's tissue culture are dividing strangely under the microscope. You have one lab session to diagnose what stage of mitosis is going wrong.

amara.name: Dr. Amara Osei
amara.description: Has spent more hours at a microscope than anyone else on staff.

theo.name: Theo
theo.description: Keeps calling every cell stage 'the splitty part.'

microscope_slide.name: Prepared Slide
microscope_slide.description: A stained tissue sample ready for viewing.

cell_atlas.name: Cell Cycle Atlas
cell_atlas.description: Reference diagrams for every phase of mitosis.

elements.text: Some of these cells aren't dividing evenly. If we don't identify the stage where it breaks down, the whole culture is at risk.
Can't we just toss the weird-looking ones and keep going?

options.text: "Let's use the cell atlas to identify exactly which phase these cells are stuck in."
"Just discard the weird ones and move on."

elements.text: Good, you've got the atlas. Let's match what we see to the correct phase.
Discarding cells without diagnosing them just hides the problem. We need the real phase.

config.question: Under the microscope, chromosomes are lined up single-file along the cell's equator. What phase is this?
config.explanation: Metaphase is defined by chromosomes aligning at the metaphase plate, the cell's equator, before separation.

config.prompt: Order the phases of mitosis from first to last.
Theo: "What's the organelle that organizes the spindle fibers pulling chromosomes apart? One word."

elements.text: We isolated the exact phase where things stall. The culture can be saved.
We got a diagnosis, eventually. Next time, start with the atlas, not the trash bin.

elements.prompt: The report is filed. What now?

options.text: Walk Theo through all four phases of mitosis so he can spot them independently.
Log off. The culture's saved, that's enough for today.

elements.text: So it's not just 'the splitty part' — every phase does something specific. Noted.

ending.title: Mitosis Hero
ending.description: Diagnosed the division anomaly and taught the team to read the cell cycle.

ending.title: Culture Saved
ending.description: The tissue culture survives. The deeper lesson can wait until tomorrow.
